newsitem.title: USA: Hot weather chases showers from U.S. Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Hot weather chases showers from U.S. Midwest.

text.p: A heat wave was forecast for the U.S. Midwest through Friday with high temperatures ranging from the low to high 90 degrees Fahrenheit area, beginning Tuesday, meteorologists said.

A narrow band of fast-moving rain showers ahead of the warmer air produced up to an inch of rain in isolated areas of central and southern Illinois on Monday before moving into Indiana where lesser amounts fell.
It didn't have enough time to produce any big rains anywhere," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
Rain was not expected to return to the Midwest until Friday when light scattered showers were forecast for eastern Iowa, and the northern sections of Illinois, Indiana and Ohio, meteorologists said.
"That front should bring a quarter to an inch (of rain) but coverage will be about 30 percent," said Tim Bowden, Weather Express Inc meteorologist.
Cooler weather should accompany the showers, with high temperatures slipping into the 80s then, forecasters said.
More scattered showers were forecast Saturday through Sunday for the Midwest, but coverage was expected to be light.
Another storm system may enter the Midwest Monday or Tuesday, July 21 or 22, which has the potential to bring rain to a broad area.
"It looks to offer a better chance of rain, possibly 1/2 to 1-1/2 inches, 60 percent coverage," said Bowden.
However, he said the latest weather maps suggest next week's storm system may weaken before it arrives.
